title: Finite-etale torsor comparison
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], let $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $Y_0=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ be its closed fibre and $i:Y_0\to Y$ the projection (a closed immersion, the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$). Let $M$ be a finite abelian group, $\underline M_Y$ and $\underline M_{Y_0}$ the constant sheaves with value $M$ on the small etale sites $Y_{\Et}$, $Y_{0,\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], $i^{-1}$ the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $c:i^{-1}\underline M_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline M_{Y_0}$ the canonical isomorphism of [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. Let

$$
 i^*:H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M_Y)\longrightarrow H^1(Y_{0,\Et},i^{-1}\underline M_Y)
$$

be the pullback map of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] between the etale cohomology groups of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and $H^1(c)$ the map induced by $c$. Then the restriction map

$$
 H^1(c)\circ i^*:H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M)\longrightarrow H^1(Y_{0,\Et},\underline M)
$$

is bijective; equivalently ($H^1(c)$ being bijective as $c$ is an isomorphism and $H^1(-)$ a functor), $i^*$ is bijective.

proof.text: *Empty fibres and base points.* If $Y=\emptyset$, then $Y_0=\emptyset$; the small etale site of the empty scheme has the single object $\emptyset$, covered by the empty family, so every abelian sheaf on it is $0$ and $H^1=0$ on both sides: the map is bijective. Let $Y\neq\emptyset$. Then $I$ lies in every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $A$: otherwise $I+\mathfrak n=A$, and the finite $A$-algebra $B=A/\mathfrak n$ has $B/IB=0$, whose idempotent $0$ has the two distinct lifts $0,1$ in the field $B$, contradicting the uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. The image $f(Y)$ is closed (proper morphisms are universally closed, [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]) and nonempty, so it contains a closed point $\mathfrak n\supseteq I$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, i.e. a point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$; a point $y\in Y$ over it and the point $\mathfrak n$ give a point of the fibre product $Y_0$ (the fibre product of the residue fields $\kappa(y)\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak n)}\kappa(\mathfrak n)$ is nonzero). So $Y_0\neq\emptyset$, and both $Y$ and $Y_0$ have geometric points (the spectrum of an algebraic closure of a residue field); fix them, so that $Y$ and $Y_0$ are in the situation of [def-galois-categories]. The base points play no role below.

source.place: Lemma 0A5G (label lemma-proper-over-henselian-and-h1): the henselian local ring of the source has its closed point in the image of every nonempty proper scheme; the pair case is written here by the agent

proof.text:
*Cohomology classes are torsors, naturally.* For $T\in\{Y,Y_0\}$ let $\operatorname{Tor}^1(T,M)$ be the set of isomorphism classes of $\underline M_T$-torsors on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors] (sheaves of sets $P$ with an $\underline M_T$-action such that $\underline M_T\times P\to P\times P$, $(m,x)\mapsto(m+x,x)$, is an isomorphism and which have sections on the members of some etale covering of $T$, Stacks 03AH (2)). By [thm-galois-torsor-h1] (Stacks 03AJ, Cohomology on Sites, Lemma torsors-h1, as used in the proof of 0A5G) there are canonical bijections $\theta_T:\operatorname{Tor}^1(T,M)\to H^1(T_{\Et},\underline M_T)$, natural in $T$. Naturality for $i:Y_0\to Y$ is the following: for an $\underline M_Y$-torsor $P$ on $Y_{\Et}$, the inverse image $i^{-1}P$ (inverse image of sheaves of sets, which commutes with finite products, so $i^{-1}\underline M_Y\times i^{-1}P\to i^{-1}P\times i^{-1}P$ is again an isomorphism, and which has sections over the pullback $\{U_k\times_YY_0\to Y_0\}$ of a covering on whose members $P$ has sections) is an $i^{-1}\underline M_Y$-torsor, an $\underline M_{Y_0}$-torsor $i^\ast P$ through the isomorphism $c$ of [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant], and

$$
 \theta_{Y_0}([i^\ast P])=H^1(c)\bigl(i^*\theta_Y([P])\bigr),
$$

with $i^*$ the pullback map of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. So $H^1(c)\circ i^*$ corresponds under $\theta_Y,\theta_{Y_0}$ to $[P]\mapsto[i^\ast P]$, and it suffices to show that this map $\operatorname{Tor}^1(Y,M)\to\operatorname{Tor}^1(Y_0,M)$ is bijective.

source.place: Lemma 0A5G (label lemma-proper-over-henselian-and-h1), proof, first sentence; literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex Definition 03AH and Lemma 03AJ (label lemma-torsors-h1)

proof.text: *Torsors are finite etale schemes with a simply transitive $M$-action.* For a scheme $T$ let $\mathrm{Et}^1(T,M)$ be the set of isomorphism classes of pairs $(V,\rho)$ with $V\to T$ finite etale and surjective and $\rho:M\to\operatorname{Aut}_T(V)$ a homomorphism such that $\sigma_V:\coprod_{m\in M}V\to V\times_TV$, equal to $(\rho(m),\mathrm{id}_V)$ on the $m$-th summand, is an isomorphism (isomorphisms of pairs: $M$-equivariant $T$-isomorphisms). By [thm-galois-lc-etale] the functor $V\mapsto h_V=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_T(-,V)$ is an equivalence $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(T)\to\mathrm{FLC}(T)$ which carries simply transitive $M$-actions to simply transitive ones and $M$-torsors to $M$-torsors and is compatible with base change; concretely $h_{\coprod_MV}=\underline M_T\times h_V$, $h_{V\times_TV}=h_V\times h_V$ and $h_{\sigma_V}$ is the action map, while $V\to T$ surjective means exactly that $h_V$ has sections locally ($V\to T$ is itself an etale covering with the tautological section over $V$; conversely sections over the members $U_k$ of a covering are $T$-maps $U_k\to V$, so the image of $V$ contains the union of the images of the $U_k$, which is $T$). Every $\underline M_T$-torsor is finite locally constant (it is locally isomorphic to $\underline M_T$), so $(V,\rho)\mapsto h_V$ is a bijection $\mathrm{Et}^1(T,M)\to\operatorname{Tor}^1(T,M)$, as in the proof of 0A5G (there through Stacks 03RV, lemma-characterize-finite-locally-constant). By the base change compatibility, $h_{V\times_YY_0}\cong i^{-1}h_V$ compatibly with the actions, the action of $\coprod_MY_0=(\coprod_MY)\times_YY_0$ matching that of $\underline M_{Y_0}$ through $c$. Hence the map $[P]\mapsto[i^\ast P]$ of the previous step corresponds to the restriction $R:\mathrm{Et}^1(Y,M)\to\mathrm{Et}^1(Y_0,M)$, $(V,\rho)\mapsto(V_0,\rho_0)=(V\times_YY_0,\rho\times_YY_0)$, and it suffices to show that $R$ is bijective.

source.place: Lemma 0A5G (label lemma-proper-over-henselian-and-h1), proof, sentences 2-5 (torsors are finite locally constant, hence representable by finite etale schemes, Lemma 03RV; conversely a finite etale scheme with an M-torsor action gives a class; the same over X_0)

proof.text: *$R$ is well defined.* Base change along $i$ preserves finite etale morphisms and surjectivity [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], sends the $Y$-automorphisms $\rho(m)$ to $Y_0$-automorphisms $\rho_0(m)$ with $\rho_0(0)=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho_0(m+n)=\rho_0(m)\rho_0(n)$, and commutes with finite coproducts and fibre products: $(\coprod_MV)\times_YY_0=\coprod_MV_0$, $(V\times_YV)\times_YY_0=V_0\times_{Y_0}V_0$, and $\sigma_V\times_YY_0=\sigma_{V_0}$, which is therefore an isomorphism. An $M$-equivariant isomorphism of pairs base-changes to one, so $R$ is a well defined map of isomorphism classes.

*$R$ is injective.* By [thm-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting] (whose hypotheses are those of this lemma) the restriction functor $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)\to\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y_0)$, $V\mapsto V_0$, is an equivalence, in particular fully faithful. Let $(V,\rho),(V',\rho')$ have $\varphi_0:(V_0,\rho_0)\xrightarrow{\sim}(V'_0,\rho'_0)$. Full faithfulness gives unique $Y$-morphisms $\varphi:V\to V'$ and $\psi:V'\to V$ restricting to $\varphi_0$ and $\varphi_0^{-1}$; $\psi\varphi$ and $\mathrm{id}_V$ both restrict to $\mathrm{id}_{V_0}$, so $\psi\varphi=\mathrm{id}$, and likewise $\varphi\psi=\mathrm{id}$. For $m\in M$ the morphisms $\varphi\rho(m)$ and $\rho'(m)\varphi$ restrict to $\varphi_0\rho_0(m)=\rho'_0(m)\varphi_0$, hence are equal by faithfulness. So $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of pairs and $R$ is injective.

source.place: Lemma 0A5G (label lemma-proper-over-henselian-and-h1), proof, last sentence (consequence of the equivalence of literature/stacks-project/pione.tex Lemma 0A48, label lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian)

proof.text: *$R$ is surjective.* Let $(W,\tau)\in\mathrm{Et}^1(Y_0,M)$. By essential surjectivity in [thm-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting] there are a finite etale $V\to Y$ and a $Y_0$-isomorphism $V_0\cong W$; transport $\tau$ to an action $\tau'$ on $V_0$. By full faithfulness each $\tau'(m)$ is the restriction of a unique $Y$-endomorphism $\rho(m)$ of $V$ (the theorem's unique lifting of finite group actions); $\rho(0)$ and $\mathrm{id}_V$, and $\rho(m+n)$ and $\rho(m)\rho(n)$, have equal restrictions, hence are equal, so $\rho:M\to\operatorname{Aut}_Y(V)$ is a homomorphism. Simple transitivity: $\coprod_MV$ and $V\times_YV$ are finite etale over $Y$ (finite coproducts and fibre products of finite etale morphisms), $\sigma_V$ is a morphism between them in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$, and its restriction $\sigma_{V_0}$ (previous step) is an isomorphism, being identified with $\sigma_W$; an equivalence reflects isomorphisms, so $\sigma_V$ is an isomorphism. Surjectivity of $\pi:V\to Y$: $\pi$ is etale, hence flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence open [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]; it is finite, hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], hence closed. So $\pi(V)$ is open and closed; let $Y'\subseteq Y$ be the open subscheme on it and $j:Y'\to Y$ the inclusion, an open and closed immersion, hence finite etale. Since $V_0\to Y_0$ is surjective and factors through $j_0:Y'\times_YY_0\to Y_0$, the open and closed immersion $j_0$ is surjective, hence an isomorphism. As the equivalence reflects isomorphisms, $j$ (a morphism $Y'\to Y$ of $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$) is an isomorphism, so $\pi$ is surjective. Thus $(V,\rho)\in\mathrm{Et}^1(Y,M)$ and $R(V,\rho)\cong(W,\tau)$.

source.place: Lemma 0A5G (label lemma-proper-over-henselian-and-h1), proof, last sentence; the lifting of the action, of simple transitivity and of surjectivity is written out by the agent

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By the last three steps $R$ is bijective; by the third step so is $[P]\mapsto[i^\ast P]$ on $\operatorname{Tor}^1$, and by the second step $H^1(c)\circ i^*=\theta_{Y_0}\circ(i^\ast)\circ\theta_Y^{-1}$ is bijective. Since $H^1(c)$ is bijective, so is $i^*$.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For a finite abelian group $M$ and proper $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$,
restriction induces a bijection

$$
H^1(Y,\underline M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(Y_0,\underline M).
$$
blueprint_sketch.proof:
An $\underline M$-torsor is a finite etale $Y$-scheme $P$ with a simply
transitive $M$-action by the finite-locally-constant equivalence. Apply the
henselian lifting lemma to lift $P$, every automorphism $m:P\to P$, and the
multiplication diagrams. Uniqueness of lifted morphisms preserves the group
law and simple transitivity. Restriction and lifting are inverse on
isomorphism classes, which is the displayed $H^1$ bijection. This is the
torsor subtree of Tag `0A5G`.
